newsitem.title: UK: UAE oil minister sees repeat of 1996 bullishness.
newsitem.headline: UAE oil minister sees repeat of 1996 bullishness.

text.p: Acting UAE Oil Minister Rakad bin Salem bin Rakad said he expected oil prices to repeat 1996's bullish performance, the OPEC News Agency reported on Wednesday.
Rakad said good demand has enabled the market to easily absorb the resumption of Iraqi oil exports.
"There are several factors that govern the oil market but I expect 1997 to be a good year in terms of prices," he told the economic weekly Emirates Today, OPECNA said.
He said the impact of Iraq's return, after an absence of more than six years because of United Nations sanctions, had not been as bearish as had been feared.
"We don't feel that exaggerated impact. In fact, the return of Iraq was no surprise and it does not cause a problem of any magnitude," he said.
"The Iraqi production of their specified quota will be gradual so that oil markets can absorb it in the same (way) as the resumption of Kuwaiti production (after the war)."

Oil prices are hovering near post Gulf War highs thanks to buoyant weather-driven demand. OPEC's reference price for a basket of seven crude on Monday hit $24.52 a barrel, well above its minimum reference price of $21.
Rakad said his country was "committed" to its 2.16 million barrel per day (bpd) OPEC quota and saw no reason to increase output for now.
"We are not planning any increase, unless necessitated by a compelling development," Rakad was quoted as saying.
